newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin defends Security Council appointment.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin defends Security Council appointment.

text.p: The Kremlin, defending its decision to appoint a controversial businessman to the powerful Security Council, on Wednesday angrily ordered the communist opposition to mind its own business.

Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, told Interfax news agency the president was constitutionally entitled to make the appointment and he accused the opposition of undermining efforts to boost cooperation among political forces.

Gennady Seleznyov, the communist head of Russia's lower house of parliament had lashed out at Yeltsin's decision to make Boris Berezovsky a deputy secretary of the Security Council and said chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais was behind the appointment.

Seleznyov, chairman of the State Duma, and Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov both called on Yeltsin to sack Chubais, whom many opposition politicians suspect of amassing too much power as the president prepares for heart surgery.
"The president's position is based on a strict observance of the Russian constitution and his adherence to the principle of separation of powers," Interfax quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying.

"The protest of the State Duma chairman comes at the moment when thanks to efforts and initiatives of the president the country has seen a movement towards consolidation of different branches of power, their cooperation in the resolution of thorny state problems," he added.

Yeltsin, whose heart operation is expected to go ahead next week, last week set up a consultative council aimed at increasing cooperation between the executive and the communist-dominated legislature.
Seleznyov said he would not work in the new council because of Chubais' alleged role in appointing Berezovsky, whose business interests range from car dealerships to television.
Chubais, along with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Yegor Stroyev, chairman of the Federation Council upper chamber, are the other members of the council's "permanent four".
